results.name: Barbell Incline Shoulders Press
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 45-degree incline. Sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and press your back firmly against the bench. Hold the barbell at shoulder level with your elbows bent and pointing down.
Press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended, keeping your wrists straight and elbows slightly bent at the top.
Slowly lower the barbell back to shoulder level with control, maintaining tension in your shoulders. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and prevent lower back strain.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you press the barbell overhead and inhale as you lower it back down.
results.description: Barbell Incline Shoulders Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Triceps, Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Silverback Shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands using an overhand grip (palms down). Your hands should be shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your torso at 45 degrees to the ground.
Start with your arms fully extended, letting the barbell hang directly below your shoulders.
Shrug your shoulders upward to your ears. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding your back during the exercise to prevent injury.
Engage your core to stabilize your torso and maintain balance throughout the movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you shrug your shoulders upward and inhaling as you lower them back down.
results.description: Barbell Silverback Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Z Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your feet slightly apart. Hold the barbell at shoulder height using an overhand grip (palms facing forward), slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight, engage your core, and ensure your chest is upright.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your arms fully, keeping your head neutral and looking forward.
Slowly lower the barbell back to shoulder height. Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions.
tips: Engage your core to stabilize your torso and maintain an upright posture.
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the barbell to maximize shoulder engagement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the bar up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
results.description: Barbell Z Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Triceps, Core.

results.name: Cable 30 Degree Shrug
instructions: Stand upright between two low cable pulleys and hold the handles at your sides with a neutral grip and your arms fully extended.
Elevate your shoulders toward your ears while keeping your arms straight and your torso still.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement while squeezing your upper back muscles.
Lower your shoulders slowly to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms fully extended throughout the exercise.
Squeeze your upper trapezius at the top of each repetition.
Keep your neck in a neutral position and look straight ahead.
Inhale as you lower your shoulders and exhale as you shrug upward.
results.description: Cable 30 Degree Shrug is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Cable Face Pull With Rope
instructions: Set a cable pulley at upper chest height and attach a rope.
Hold the rope ends with an overhand grip and step back until your arms are straight.
Pull the rope toward your face, separating the ends and driving your elbows out and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades, then return slowly and repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows high.
Finish with your hands beside your ears.
results.description: Cable Face Pull With Rope is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps, Rotator Cuff.

results.name: Cable Single Arm Reverse Fly
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with the pulley set at shoulder height and hold the handle with the arm farthest from the machine. Extend your arm across the front of your body with a slight bend in your elbow.
Pull the handle outward and backward in a wide horizontal arc until your arm is in line with your shoulder.
Pause briefly while squeezing your posterior deltoid.
Slowly return the handle along the same arc to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbow throughout the exercise.
Keep your torso upright and avoid rotating as you pull.
Control the return phase to maintain constant muscle tension.
Inhale as you return to the starting position and exhale as you pull the handle outward.
results.description: Cable Single Arm Reverse Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Middle Back, Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Alternating Arnold Press
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing your body and your elbows bent.
Press one dumbbell overhead while rotating your hand until your palm faces forward as your arm reaches full extension.
Lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height while rotating your hand until your palm faces your body again.
Repeat the movement with the opposite arm, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the non-working dumbbell at shoulder height while pressing the opposite arm.
Rotate your hand smoothly throughout the press instead of turning it all at once.
Press the dumbbell directly overhead without letting your elbow flare excessively.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbell and exhale as you press it overhead.
results.description: Dumbbell Alternating Arnold Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Chest Supported Y Raise
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest fully supported. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, in a neutral grip and allow your arms to hang straight toward the floor with a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise both dumbbells diagonally upward and outward, while rotating the weight until your arms form a Y shape with your body, finishing the movement with palms facing down.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chest in contact with the bench throughout the exercise.
Use light weights to maintain proper technique and a full range of motion.
Avoid swinging the dumbbells or using momentum.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you raise them.
results.description: Dumbbell Chest Supported Y Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Rotator Cuff, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Laying 30 Degree Shrug
instructions: Lie on your right side on a 30 degree incline bench with your knees bent. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand using a neutral grip and let your arm hang straight toward the floor.
Keep your arm straight and raise your working shoulder toward your ear, lifting the dumbbell slightly upward.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back while keeping your torso still.
Slowly lower your shoulder until your arm hangs fully extended, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep the side of your torso firmly supported on the incline bench.
Keep your elbow straight and avoid curling the dumbbell.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your shoulder slowly through the full range of motion.
Exhale as you raise your shoulder and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Laying 30 Degree Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Laying Silverback Shrug
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest supported, your legs extended, and your feet firmly on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip and let your arms hang straight below your shoulders.
Shrug your shoulders toward your ears and slightly backward while keeping your arms straight and your chest against the bench.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back muscles.
Slowly lower your shoulders to the starting position, allowing them to fully relax before repeating.
tips: Keep your chest firmly supported on the bench throughout the exercise.
Move your shoulders upward and slightly backward without rolling them.
Avoid swinging the dumbbells or using momentum to lift them.
Exhale as you raise your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Laying Silverback Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Forearms.
